newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah lower on central bank fixing.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah lower on central bank fixing.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah edged down slightly against the dollar in slow late trading on Wednesday following a surprise higher central bank fixing, dealers said.
They said operators were surprised by the central bank move to raise its intervention rate by one point to 2,322/2,514 and the conversion rate to 2,322/2,370 late on Wednesday.
"It has caught the market by surprise. Nobody has expected the central bank would raise the band again today," one said.
"The central bank wants to really challenge the market as it has indicated last week," one U.S. bank dealer said.
Spot rupiah was quoted at 2,322.25/22.75 at 0900 GMT against an opening of 2,321.5/22.0. Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,321.5/22.2 and 2,320.6/21.0, respectively.
But dealers said operators did not sell any dollars to the central bank this afternoon because spot dollars were trading above the 2,322.0 level due to ample rupiah liquidity.
"The market was surprised and operators made an immediate adjustment to the fixing," one Japanese bank dealer said.
The central bank raised its fixing by one point on Tuesday, causing it to absorb some $400 million from the market to keep the dollar trading within the confined eight percent band.
"I don't think anybody sold any dollars to the bank today. Sentiment on the dollar appears to be on an upturn following a turnaround in money market liquidity," one dealer said.
"The higher fixing seems to have two meanings. It's to challenge the market or to speed up depreciation. But I think it's more likely that the central bank wants to challenge the market," he said.

Economists said earlier the central bank would have no problem in supporting the dollar if it did touch its floor rate because it could neutralise additional monetary supply through short-term securities (SBIs).
They said outstanding SBIs were much lower now compared to last year's level and M2 money supply aggregates had fallen.
Dealers said anticipation of ample liquidity in the money market seemed to help a firmer tone on the dollar.
The U.S. bank dealer said there was some upside momentum for the dollar in the short-term on liquidity factors.
"There is no room for further declines. People are looking for reasons to buy dollars for now," he said.
Dealers said liquidity was expected to be ample on Thursday but it may turn tight again on Friday.
They said short-dated swap rates had declined below the strong support level of 0.5 points, with overnight swap quoting at 0.35/0.45 and tom/next at 0.3/0.4 points.
Overnight money fell to seven percent late on Wednesday from 10.0/11.0 percent, driving short-dated swaps lower.
One-month swap fell to 17.0/18.0 from 18.00/18.75, two to 32.5/34.0 from 33.0/35.0, three to 52.5/53.5 from 52.5/54.0 and six to 102.0/103.0 from 102.25/103.25 points.
